policy: responseFormatPattern is ECMAScript source and patternFlags a subset of ims; the pattern is tested as written, without anchors. It is translated to an equivalent Python expression evaluated on UTF-16 code units. Patterns that Python cannot match identically are rejected; every accepted pattern is valid ECMAScript with the same meaning.

translated.note: Named groups and references become (?P<n>...) and (?P=n).
A reference to a group that did not participate matches the empty string: (?(1)\1).
A reference before its group closes matches the empty string: (?:).
Any character: [\s\S]. The empty class [] never matches: (?!).
A dash next to a class escape is a literal dash.
Control escapes become the control character.
Numbers above the group count are legacy octal escapes; \8 and \9 are digits.
Identity escapes of letters (\A, \Z, \z, \a, \e, \p, \N, \U, incomplete \x and \u) are the letter itself.
\S inside a class is expanded with an alternation.
A brace that is not a quantifier is a literal brace.
\B is expanded because before Python 3.14 it never matches an empty string.
Excludes \n, \r, \u2028 and \u2029; $ is end of input.
The ECMAScript whitespace set, including U+00A0 and U+FEFF; \d and \w stay ASCII.
Astral characters are two UTF-16 code units, as in ECMAScript without the u flag.

urls.policy: images[].url follows Zod's url(), which accepts what new URL() parses (WHATWG URL Standard, no base).
urls.divergence: Domains with non-ASCII characters are mapped with Python's IDNA 2003 codec instead of UTS #46, so a few unusual internationalized hosts may be accepted or rejected differently.
